svg.title: Hands-free voice: persistent intent and bounded listening
svg.desc: Hands-free is off by default. Deliberate Enable authorizes a gateway supervisor to start bounded SIP wake sessions. Actual readiness requires matching policy and session IDs, running and active status, no error or Stop, positive remaining time, and the armed wake_ready phase. The supervisor stops its own session five seconds before its deadline, confirms cleanup and observes all lines idle twice before renewing. Setup and warmup can leave capture gaps. Only positively observed ordinary-call preemption permits resumption. Uncertain cleanup faults without retry. Disable turns off desired intent before stopping the current session; a historical session Stop cannot disable a newer generation.
svg.text: Hands-free: enabled is intent, ready is a live state
Remote control · stock SIP phone · local wake detection · selected Home Assistant voice pipeline
Synthetic example line. Enable grants persistent microphone operation.
The gateway owns renewal; no CLI loop.
Enabled alone never proves active listening.
This state alone does not prove
an ordinary call is in progress.
A running process is not enough.
Never overlap or clear a lease.
Renew only after cleanup + two fresh idle observations
New call and model warmup can leave capture gaps. Renewal is not seamless listening.
Positive competing-call evidence permits later resumption.
Wait for confirmed cleanup and fresh idle observations.
Peer hangup, DTMF Stop or an ambiguous call change disables
intent instead. Do not infer permission to redial from a missing call.
Failures do not justify endless retries
backoff: bounded retries after clean transient failures
faulted: resolve the cause, then deliberately Enable again
Uncertain cleanup or ownership fails closed.
A restart does not erase unresolved state.
Desired off first, then Stop the owned session.
Check disabled intent AND confirmed session cleanup.
Stop of the current supervised session also disables intent.
A historical Stop cannot disable a newer generation.
Disabled intent alone is not proof the microphone is off.
Implementation flow, not physical acceptance. No barge-in, nearest-microphone election or guaranteed acoustic performance.
